title: Why Germany Isn’t Punishing Russia Harder
gist: Germany's response to the Leipzig drone attack — diplomatic closures, travel restrictions, a push for EU sanctions — is constrained by the AfD polling at 28% versus the CDU's 24%, Die Linke at 11%, and persistent German nuclear anxiety. Russia conducted 151 hostile operations in Europe between February 2022 and February 2026, with 144 drone sightings over a dozen states since August 2024, and officials are now reaching for the label 'state-sponsored terrorism.'

themes.theme: Domestic politics as the binding constraint

insights.claim: The AfD polled at 28 percent in April versus the ruling CDU's 24 percent, with far-left Die Linke at 11 percent — meaning roughly 39 percent of German voters back parties that have taken pro-Russian stances, and the AfD has now won its first state election.
insights.speaker: Sam Skove, John Haltiwanger
insights.so_what: German Russia policy has a hard electoral ceiling — do not model German escalation capacity off its economic weight; the political constraint binds first.
insights.locator: In April, Germany’s far-right Alternative for Germany

insights.claim: German nuclear anxiety remains a live political force that Russia has proved willing to manipulate, and Chancellor Friedrich Merz's popularity is plummeting despite broad support for Ukraine.
insights.speaker: Sam Skove, John Haltiwanger
insights.so_what: Escalation fear plus a weakening chancellor means Berlin will under-respond to future incidents — a persistent source of European deterrence shortfall.
insights.quote: This nuclear angst is still there in Germany
insights.locator: And despite broad support for Ukraine

insights.claim: German far-left representatives openly reject the government's attribution, with Die Linke parliamentarian Lea Reisner writing that 'intelligence information and plausibility are not evidence' and calling the escalation highly dangerous.
insights.speaker: Sam Skove, John Haltiwanger
insights.so_what: Attribution itself is politically contested inside Germany, which limits the domestic mandate for sanctions or retaliation.
insights.quote: Intelligence information and plausibility are not evidence
insights.locator: Many AfD and Die Linke voters

insights.claim: Germany has a pattern of muted response: after a reported Russian plot to assassinate Rheinmetall chief Armin Papperger, head of Germany's largest arms company, Berlin announced no specific punishments and then-Chancellor Scholz made no direct comment.
insights.speaker: Sam Skove, John Haltiwanger
insights.so_what: European defense-company executives face a documented assassination threat with no state deterrent response — a direct security cost line for the sector.
insights.locator: Germany’s response has appeared relatively muted

themes.theme: The scale of the Russian campaign

insights.claim: Russia conducted 151 hostile operations in Europe between its February 2022 invasion and February 2026, according to the International Centre for Counter-Terrorism.
insights.speaker: Sam Skove, John Haltiwanger
insights.so_what: Roughly one operation every ten days across four years establishes this as a sustained campaign, not episodic incidents — a permanent European security cost.
insights.quote: Russia conducted 151 hostile operations in Europe
insights.locator: But even after such steps and warnings

insights.claim: There were 144 reported drone sightings over a dozen European states between August 2024 and February 2026, with the IISS concluding it is highly likely the Kremlin conducted a UAV campaign over Europe.
insights.speaker: Sam Skove, John Haltiwanger
insights.so_what: A confirmed systematic drone campaign across Europe underpins sustained counter-UAS procurement demand and rising airport and infrastructure disruption risk.
insights.quote: it is highly likely that the Kremlin conducted a UAV campaign over Europe

insights.claim: Germany has been a priority target, with plots including the planned assassinations of a major German arms CEO and a German drone company CEO, and a scheme to send mail bombs via a German parcel carrier.
insights.speaker: Sam Skove, John Haltiwanger
insights.so_what: Parcel and logistics networks are an identified attack vector — an operational and insurance risk for European carriers beyond the defense sector.
insights.locator: Instances of Russian sabotage and other forms

insights.claim: Ursula von der Leyen characterized Leipzig as an attack using military-grade material carried out by Russian operatives on EU soil, marking 'a new escalation on European soil, directly attributed to Russia.'
insights.speaker: Sam Skove, John Haltiwanger
insights.so_what: EU-level attribution at the Commission president's level raises the probability of a coordinated sanctions package beyond German bilateral measures.
insights.quote: This was an attack using military-grade material, carried out by Russian operatives on EU soil. And we will not tolerate it.
insights.locator: “This was an attack using military-grade material

insights.claim: A more robust German response could include seizing the ships Russia uses to evade energy sanctions — as other countries already do — and offensive cyberattacks, which would legally require parliamentary sign-off.
insights.speaker: Sam Skove, John Haltiwanger
insights.so_what: Shadow-fleet seizure is the most economically material escalation option available; if Germany joins other states in doing it, Russian crude logistics costs rise materially.
insights.locator: A more robust response from Germany

insights.claim: Germany declined to invoke NATO Article 4 over Leipzig, despite it having been invoked twice in September 2025 alone over Russian drone and fighter incursions into Polish and Estonian airspace — a step taken only nine times since 1949.
insights.speaker: Sam Skove, John Haltiwanger
insights.so_what: Germany setting a higher Article 4 bar than Poland or Estonia signals divergent alliance thresholds — a fault line Moscow can probe.
insights.locator: One action Germany declined to take

insights.claim: Liana Fix judges that Germany's response resembles its pre-2022 posture and does not rise to the moment of Russian hybrid campaigns, while Ben Wallace warns that inaction guarantees repetition.
insights.speaker: Sam Skove, John Haltiwanger
insights.so_what: Expert consensus is that current deterrence is failing, implying incident frequency continues rising — plan for more, not fewer, European disruptions.
insights.quote: It does not rise to the moment of Russian hybrid campaigns.
insights.locator: Many commentators have slammed Germany’s response

themes.theme: Relabeling hybrid warfare as state terrorism

insights.claim: EU foreign-policy chief Kaja Kallas said the failed attack 'has all the hallmarks of state-sponsored terrorism,' and Estonia's Margus Tsahkna argues the label matters because states already know how to act against terrorism.
insights.speaker: Sam Skove, John Haltiwanger
insights.so_what: A terrorism designation would unlock existing counterterrorism legal and financial tools against Russian entities — a materially different sanctions regime than current measures.
insights.quote: has all the hallmarks of state-sponsored terrorism

insights.claim: Doug Lute notes the terrorism framing is an interesting escalation because the only Article 5 invocation in NATO history followed the 9/11 terror attacks — implicitly linking the label to collective-defense thresholds.
insights.speaker: Sam Skove, John Haltiwanger
insights.so_what: If hybrid attacks get classified as terrorism, the precedent creates a pathway to Article 5 — a significant widening of escalation risk in Europe.

insights.claim: Lute argues NATO must stop treating Russian hybrid attacks as one-offs and instead compile the accumulated record, because there is power in assembling them into a package that shows the breadth, depth and persistence of the campaign.
insights.speaker: Sam Skove, John Haltiwanger
insights.so_what: Aggregated attribution is the precondition for a collective response — watch for a NATO compiled-incident report as the trigger for coordinated action.
insights.quote: There’s power in accumulating them and assembling them into a package so that you can see the breadth and depth and the persistence of the attacks

insights.claim: Estonia views the German attribution as the key change because it publicly disproves the narrative that Russian attacks are only a Baltic concern, though Tsahkna concedes it is hard to define a proportional response and rules out reciprocal attacks.
insights.speaker: Sam Skove, John Haltiwanger
insights.so_what: Broadening the perceived target set from the Baltics to Western Europe is what would mobilize larger European defense budgets — that shift is now underway.
insights.quote: it’s now “public for everybody in Europe that Russia is attacking Germany and attacking many other countries as well.
insights.locator: There’s been a narrative that the “Baltics are next”
